text:
maya: Heads-up: AcmeCorp just escalated — their generation quality dropped after the 03:10 deploy. They say outputs got "more creative" and factually wrong. Example attached in thread. Marking P1 for now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] prod/model-serving v2.14.0 rolled at 2024-06-30T03:10:12Z by ci-release (commit abc123). Changes: sampling defaults refactor.

maya: Customer repro (redacted ids):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-13b","input":"Summarize the policy doc.", "max_tokens":120 }'
```
They say the same prompt that used to produce conservative summaries now returns hallucinated recommendations.

aj: Looking. I pulled logs for the customer requests around deploy time. Their requests are exactly the simple payload above (no temperature/top_p). Pre-deploy responses had temperature effectively ~0.15 in practice. Post-deploy looks like temperature ~0.75.

sam: that's bad. any config change in runtime?

aj: Found the PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serving/pulls/4321 — title "unify sampling defaults across runtimes". The change centralizes defaults into runtime/serve/config.go. Previously models had explicit defaults set in model profiles. The new code falls back to a global default if both temp/top_p omitted. The global default got set to temp=0.8, top_p=1.0 in the refactor.

aj: Diff snippet:
```diff
- // previous per-model defaults
- modelDefaults: { temperature: 0.2, top_p: 0.95 }
+ // refactor: global default
+ globalSamplingDefault: { temperature: 0.8, top_p: 1.0 }
```

lucy: Wait, that PR passed QA? It should have been a behavioral change. We should have flagged this.

maya: Customer is requesting rollback or hotfix ASAP. They're on a paid enterprise contract.

sam: Can we hotfix by patching runtime to preserve per-model defaults if present in model catalog? If we can flip the global default back to 0.2 quickly that might mitigate.

aj: Two mitigation options: 1) Roll back the deploy (fastest) — but it's a large release including other fixes. 2) Patch runtime to explicitly prefer model profile defaults when available, and set global default to previous conservative values. I can prepare a patch and hotfix in ~30-45m if we approve.

lucy: Product prefer patch instead of full rollback to avoid losing other critical fixes. Also need comms to affected customers.

maya: For AcmeCorp, temporary workaround: instruct them to set temperature=0.2 top_p=0.95 in the request body. They'll need a code change on their side but it's immediate. I'll send them that and an apology.

aj: Repro steps for QA: run batch script hitting same model with omitted sampling vs explicit low sampling and diff outputs. Example fuzz test I ran shows KL divergence jump > 0.8 after deploy, and factuality score drop on our eval set (policy-summary) from 0.93 to 0.71.

aj: Current logs (snippet):
```
[2024-06-30T03:12:05Z] req_id=xyz user=acme op=generate model=gptx-13b sampling:temperature=0.8 top_p=1.0
[2024-06-30T03:12:05Z] req_id=xyz output=... WARNING: low factuality score=0.42
```

sam: I'm pinging infra to hold further rollout / pause the canary expansion.

deploy-bot: [action] paused canary expansion for prod/model-serving by sam @ 2024-06-30T04:05:00Z

aj: Draft hotfix PR ready: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serving/pulls/4330 — "preserve model profile sampling defaults; set global default to 0.2". Tests passing locally. Needs +1 from eng-runtime and a quick canary.

lucy: Also add a note to release notes and update breaking-changes doc. This is a behavioral change that could surprise customers.

maya: Customer update I sent: "We're investigating — immediate workaround: include temperature=0.2 and top_p=0.95 in your generation requests. We will roll a hotfix within the hour and follow up with postmortem." They replied they can do the workaround but want a timeline.

aj: Action items:
- aj: push hotfix canary (target +10% traffic) and monitor KL/factuality metrics — ETA 45m
- sam: keep canary paused until canary config changed, coordinate with infra
- maya: patch customer comms and capture examples for postmortem
- lucy: draft external comms if more customers affected

maya: Noted. Also logging request: add telemetry to distinguish omitted-sampling vs explicit-sampling to find who else is impacted historically.

aj: Will add telemetry flag and a mass-run to scan last 7 days for requests that omitted sampling fields. Early estimate: ~12 customers at scale might be affected, mostly enterprise customers that rely on conservative defaults.

sam: Filing an incident in incidents channel, tagging SEC/Legal for enterprise SLA/legal implications.

lucy: We should also consider a product change: never change global behavior without opt-in or a major version bump. Documenting in runbooks.

maya: OK — I'll keep thread updated.

aj: Hotfix merged at 2024-06-30T04:40:12Z, canary applied to 10% traffic. Initial metrics: factuality on policy-summary eval back to 0.91 for canary, KL divergence drops to baseline.

maya: AcmeCorp confirmed improved outputs when they tried the workaround and said they'll wait for full rollout.

deploy-bot: [deploy] prod/model-serving v2.14.1 hotfix (commit def456) rolled canary 10% at 2024-06-30T04:41:00Z by ci-hotfix

sam: Great. Leaving canary for 30m then we'll promote if stable.

lucy: Postmortem actions: include a policy for sampling default changes, require a QA run on canonical prompts for every behavioral change, and add a feature flag around global default refactor.

maya: Thanks team. I'll follow up with AcmeCorp and update the incident ticket.

aj: Filed PR for telemetry and audit logs as follow-up. We'll schedule a postmortem tomorrow.

sam: noted.

maya: Closing notes: root cause = sampling defaults refactor that introduced a more permissive global default (temp=0.8/top_p=1.0) which applied when clients omitted sampling fields; fix = hotfix preserving per-model defaults and revert global default to conservative values; customer mitigation = explicit sampling in request.

lucy: +1 on postmortem and product policy changes.

maya: End of thread — updating incident ticket now.
